body:
Codex dispositions on the existing review

The Narrative Codex changes the center of gravity in a useful way: the first product slice should now be a canonical evidentiary view, not an Atlas tracer. I agree with nearly all of the proposed dispositions, with one structural correction.

A1 ACCEPT WITH REVISION. Keep the portable visualization semantics in storymodel4s until the seams stabilize, and keep the browser application outside the library. Now that one canonical output is annotated text rather than geometric marks, I would start with a top-level portable view module rather than naming the whole seam scene. It can own shared view state, CodexFlow, NarrativeScene, audit records, and view laws. NarrativeScene is the Atlas-specific geometric algebra inside that module. An Intaglio adapter can remain a JVM and Scala.js backend without imposing that platform limit on the pure types.

A2 ACCEPT. The currently empty codec seam is the first transport contract. It should encode validated model inputs and serializable view specifications and outputs, but view compilation itself must not depend on codec.

A3 ACCEPT. There should be one read model and one audit vocabulary, with Atlas and Codex consuming it. A third browser-specific read contract would guarantee drift.

A4 ACCEPT THE REQUIREMENT, REJECT A SINGLE CLOSED ADT IN CORE OR STORY. The current dependency graph makes a closed NarrativeRef containing features, story nodes, recall units, and align cells cyclic: core cannot name upper modules, story cannot name recall or align, and align already depends on story and recall. Put a typed address protocol and stable module discriminator in core; each module defines its own opaque typed address or tag. Assemble an existential or coproduct address only at the top-level view and wire boundary. The view-facing address must still serialize canonically and round-trip, but lower modules must not import the universe of narrative object types.

A5 ACCEPT. Default compilers consume Validated or Adjudicated models. Draft and unresolved material needs an explicit diagnostic mode and visible status chrome; it cannot silently enter a normal view.

P1 ACCEPT. Chronology is a per-context partial-order layout with uncertainty and incomparability, not a fake real-valued world-time coordinate. A metric axis is only available when the input model actually supplies one.

P2 ACCEPT. Discourse anchoring should use a declared anchor such as first supported span or first discourse occurrence. Discontinuous later support becomes a portal or tether, never a center-of-hull coordinate.

P3 ACCEPT. Narrative containment and surface granularity are distinct axes. The default drill path may pair them, but the type system and UI must permit, for example, event structure over a sentence-scale text view.

E1 ACCEPT. Reader-time filtering requires transitive evidence closure, time-indexed identity resolution, incomplete feature windows, and no future right-context evidence. It is a different build, not a simple visibility predicate over the omniscient result.

U1 AND U2 ACCEPT. Raw scores, calibrated probabilities, coverage, missingness, alternatives, unresolved states, and policy exclusions need separate representations. Every geometric or aggregate mark needs an inspectable textual twin.

R1, F1, F2 ACCEPT. Recall rendering vocabulary must be derived from the actual alignment state algebra. Feature views compile existing derivations, window bases, reducers, coverage, and rankings. Circularity status from FeatureUseLedger must travel with every displayed aggregate.

S1 ACCEPT. No tile pyramid before a measured corpus-scale failure. Preserve a tile-compatible scene boundary, but do not build infrastructure to a conjectured bottleneck.

S2 ACCEPT WITH SCOPE. SVG-first is right for Atlas marks, Codex gutters and overlays, deterministic export, and accessibility hooks. Exact prose remains DOM text. Dense scalar underlays can move to Canvas only after a benchmark demonstrates the need.

S3 ACCEPT. Layout output is scientific state. Any JS-only layout used experimentally must be seeded, versioned, receipted, and reproducible, or it is not a publication backend.

Q1 AND B4 ACCEPT STRONGLY. The first vertical slice is the textual observatory, now explicitly the Narrative Codex. An inspectable static HTML edition is the first acceptance artifact. A two-level zoom tracer remains a useful boundary experiment but is not the first product milestone.

B1 ACCEPT. Do not design a general 2D engine in advance. Begin with a minimal renderer protocol: grouped marks, affine transform, bounds, viewport query, hit testing, and export. Dogfood Intaglio behind it. Promote only demonstrated general mechanisms such as stable bounds, camera transforms, culling, scale visibility, path geometry, and scalar fields.

B2 AND B3 ACCEPT. View compilers render accepted model semantics; they do not infer missing events or relations. Recall visuals are generated from AlignState and its mass and uncertainty quantities, not from an independent illustration vocabulary.

Proposed dependency direction

  core typed address protocol
       ^
  domain modules define local address tags
       ^
  view consumes validated domain models and produces CodexFlow or NarrativeScene
       ^
  codec serializes inputs, view specs, outputs, and receipts
       ^
  browser app uses DOM plus Intaglio SVG and optional Canvas adapters

That preserves lift-out potential without pretending that story-independent rendering abstractions are already known.
